Why the endings carry the leverage:
The argument of this module, stated once: most Greek spelling decisions are grammar, and grammar is learnable, so most of the spelling burden is not memory at all.

**The problem, restated from Spelling 1.** Five vowel sounds and a dozen spellings. **ι η υ ει οι υι** all say *i*; **ε** and **αι** both say *e*; **ο** and **ω** both say *o*. Which spelling a word takes is inherited from Ancient Greek and is a fact about that word.

**The leverage.** That is true of **roots**. It is not true of **endings**:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Roots** | arbitrary, inherited, and must be learned one word at a time |
| **Endings** | **regular, and decided by the grammar** |

**And endings are where most of the letters are.** Every noun, adjective and verb in every sentence carries one, so the same twenty endings recur thousands of times a page. **Getting the endings right removes the large majority of your spelling errors**, and getting them right is a grammar exercise rather than a memory task.

**The worked example, which is the whole module in miniature:**

> You hear **kalí**. Four spellings are possible: **καλή, καλί, καλεί, καλοί**.

**The grammar decides:**

| Spelling | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| **καλή** | feminine singular adjective — *a good woman* |
| **καλοί** | masculine plural adjective — *good men* |
| **καλεί** | the verb **καλώ** in the third person — *he calls* |
| **καλί** | **not a word** |

**So you do not have to remember which *i* the word takes. You have to know what the word is doing in the sentence**, and you have known that since stage 3.

**The second worked example, the commonest error of all:**

> **να γράφει** or **να γράφη**?

**Always -ει.** The verb's third-person singular ending is **-ει** in every mood. **να γράφη** is a katharevousa form that modern orthography abolished, and it is the single most frequent mistake made by learners and by Greeks.

**The four rules this module teaches**, each with a lesson:

1. **The nominative endings** by gender — which decide the commonest *i* and *o* choices.
2. **The genitive and the plural** — **-ου, -ης, -ας, -ιού** and **-οι, -ες, -α, -η**.
3. **The adjective endings**, including the awkward **-ής / -ιά / -ί** group.
4. **The verb endings**, which are the next module.

**What this module does not cover.** The roots. **αυγό or αβγό, τραίνο or τρένο, αυτί with αυ** — those are word facts, they go on cards, and Spelling 4 handles the patterns among them.

**The method for this module.** Each lesson is a table plus a drill, and the drill is always the same shape: **a sentence with the ending blanked, which you fill by naming the grammar.**

> Η καλ__ γυναίκα → **καλή** (feminine nominative singular)
> Οι καλ__ άνθρωποι → **καλοί** (masculine nominative plural)
> Αυτός καλ__ τον γιατρό → **καλεί** (third person singular verb)

**Say the reason out loud as you write it.** The reason is what transfers; the answer is not.

**Practice.** Take one page of Greek and underline every ending — every noun, adjective and verb ending in the page. Then for ten of them, say out loud why that ending and not another. That is the exercise this whole module consists of.
The masculine endings:
Every masculine noun ending, with its spelling, and the rule for each.

**The nominative singular**, which is how a noun is listed:

| Ending | Example | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ος** | **ο άνθρωπος, ο δρόμος, ο ουρανός** | **ο, not ω.** The commonest masculine ending. |
| **-ης** | **ο μαθητής, ο ναύτης, ο εργάτης** | **η, not ι or ει** |
| **-ας** | **ο πατέρας, ο άντρας, ο χειμώνας** | **α** |
| **-ές** | **ο καφές, ο καναπές** | loanwords, mostly |
| **-ους** | **ο παππούς, ο νους** | few |
| **-έας** | **ο συγγραφέας, ο ιερέας, ο κουρέας** | the agent nouns |
| **-ωνας** | **ο αγώνας, ο χειμώνας, ο κανόνας** | **ω** in the stem |

**The two to get right every time: -ος with omicron, -ης with eta.** Between them they cover most masculine nouns in the language.

**The vocative**, which the email lesson needed:

| Nominative | Vocative |
| --- | --- |
| **-ος** | **-ε** — ο Νίκος → **Νίκο**; ο Παπαδόπουλος → **Παπαδόπουλε** |
| **-ης** | **-η** — ο Γιάννης → **Γιάννη** |
| **-ας** | **-α** — ο πατέρας → **πατέρα** |
| **-έας** | **-έα** — ο ιερέας → **ιερέα** |

**The genitive singular:**

| Type | Genitive | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ος** | **-ου** — του ανθρώπου | **ου** |
| **-ης** | **-η** — του μαθητή | **η**, with no **ς** |
| **-ας** | **-α** — του πατέρα | **α** |
| **-έας** | **-έα** — του συγγραφέα | |
| **-ους** | **-ού** — του παππού | |

**Note the -ης genitive: του μαθητή**, not **-ή̈ς** and not **-ί**. **The genitive of an -ης noun loses the ς and keeps the η.**

**The nominative plural, which is the big *i* decision:**

| Type | Plural | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ος** | **-οι** — οι άνθρωποι | **οι — and never -ι or -η** |
| **-ης** | **-ες** — οι μαθητές | **ε** |
| **-ας** | **-ες** — οι πατέρες | **ε** |
| **-έας** | **-είς** — οι συγγραφείς | **ει**, and learned |
| **-ωνας** | **-ωνες** — οι αγώνες | |
| **-ους** | **-ούδες / -οι** — οι παππούδες | |

**οι άνθρωποι with -οι is the rule to drill.** Every masculine **-ος** noun makes its plural in **-οι**, and so does every masculine **-ος** adjective: **οι καλοί άνθρωποι**.

**The accusative:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Singular** | drop the **ς**: τον άνθρωπο, τον μαθητή, τον πατέρα |
| **Plural** | same as the nominative plural: τους ανθρώπους — **and note the -ους here, with ς** |

**The genitive plural**, which is **-ων** for everything:

> **των ανθρώπων, των μαθητών, των πατέρων, των αγώνων**

**-ων with omega, always.** The genitive plural ending has no alternative spelling, which makes it the easiest ending in the language.

**The full table for one noun, as a model:**

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom.** | ο άνθρωπος | οι άνθρωποι |
| **Gen.** | του ανθρώπου | των ανθρώπων |
| **Acc.** | τον άνθρωπο | τους ανθρώπους |
| **Voc.** | άνθρωπε | άνθρωποι |

**Practice.** Write out the full table for **ο μαθητής**, **ο πατέρας** and **ο συγγραφέας** from memory, then check them. Then take ten masculine nouns from today's reading and write their plurals, saying the rule aloud.
The feminine endings:
Every feminine ending, which is where the *i* problem is heaviest — because **-η** and **-α** are both common and both have alternatives that are wrong.

**The nominative singular:**

| Ending | Example | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-η** | **η νίκη, η αγάπη, η τιμή** | **η — not ι, not ει, not οι** |
| **-α** | **η ώρα, η γλώσσα, η καρδιά** | **α** |
| **-ος** | **η οδός, η μέθοδος, η είσοδος** | **feminine in -ος**, and learned. Declines like a masculine. |
| **-ού** | **η αλεπού, η μαϊμού** | few |
| **-η (learned)** | **η πόλη, η δύναμη, η τάξη** | the **-ις** nouns, modernised |

**The feminine -ος group is worth flagging** because the ending looks masculine: **η οδός, η νήσος, η ψήφος, η είσοδος, η έξοδος, η μέθοδος, η περίοδος, η διάμετρος**. They take feminine articles and masculine-shaped endings, and they are all learned vocabulary.

**The genitive singular:**

| Type | Genitive | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-η** | **-ης** — της νίκης | **η**, plus **ς** |
| **-α** | **-ας** — της ώρας | **α**, plus **ς** |
| **-η (πόλη type)** | **-ης** — της πόλης | and **της πόλεως** in the learned register |
| **-ος** | **-ού** — της οδού | |

**The nominative plural:**

| Type | Plural | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-η** | **-ες** — οι νίκες | **ε** |
| **-α** | **-ες** — οι ώρες | **ε** |
| **-η (πόλη type)** | **-εις** — **οι πόλεις, οι δυνάμεις, οι τάξεις** | **ει — and this is the exception to learn** |
| **-ος** | **-οι** — οι οδοί | |

**οι πόλεις with -εις is the one irregularity in the feminine system that matters.** The **-ση / -ξη / -ψη** nouns — which stage 9's nominalisation lesson showed are the backbone of written Greek — all belong to this group:

> **η απόφαση → οι αποφάσεις**
> **η ανακοίνωση → οι ανακοινώσεις**
> **η αύξηση → οι αυξήσεις**
> **η τάξη → οι τάξεις**
> **η δύναμη → οι δυνάμεις**

**So the single highest-value feminine rule is: an abstract noun in -ση makes its plural in -σεις.**

**The accusative:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Singular** | the same as the nominative: την νίκη, την ώρα, την πόλη |
| **Plural** | the same as the nominative plural: τις νίκες, τις ώρες, **τις πόλεις** |

**The feminine accusative singular equals the nominative**, which removes one decision entirely.

**The genitive plural: -ων, as always.**

> **των νικών, των ωρών, των πόλεων** — and note **πόλεων**, which keeps the learned **-εων**.

**The full tables:**

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom.** | η νίκη | οι νίκες |
| **Gen.** | της νίκης | των νικών |
| **Acc.** | τη(ν) νίκη | τις νίκες |

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom.** | η πόλη | οι πόλεις |
| **Gen.** | της πόλης | των πόλεων |
| **Acc.** | την πόλη | τις πόλεις |

**And the spelling test that catches most feminine errors**, in two questions:

1. **Is it singular or plural?** Singular **-η** or **-α**; plural **-ες** (or **-εις** for the **-ση** group).
2. **Is it genitive?** Then add **ς** in the singular and use **-ων** in the plural.

**Practice.** Write the full tables for **η ώρα**, **η απόφαση** and **η οδός**. Then take fifteen feminine nouns from today's reading, write their plurals, and check that every **-ση** made **-σεις**.
The neuter endings:
Every neuter ending — and the neuter is the easiest gender to spell, because the nominative and the accusative are identical in both numbers.

**The nominative singular:**

| Ending | Example | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ο** | **το βιβλίο, το δώρο, το πρόσωπο** | **ο, not ω** |
| **-ι** | **το παιδί, το σπίτι, το χέρι** | **ι — not η, not ει, not οι** |
| **-μα** | **το γράμμα, το μάθημα, το πρόβλημα** | **the -ματα group** |
| **-ος** | **το μέρος, το δάσος, το έθνος** | **neuter in -ος**, and learned |
| **-ιμο** | **το κλείσιμο, το άνοιγμα** | the verbal nouns |
| **-ας / -αν** | **το κρέας, το τέρας, το φως** | a handful of irregulars |

**The -ι group is the one to drill**, because the sound is *i* and **ι** is the only correct spelling: **το παιδί, το σπίτι, το κλειδί, το τραπέζι, το μάτι, το αυτί, το ψωμί, το κρασί, το χέρι, το πόδι**. **No neuter noun ends in -η or -ει.**

**The genitive singular:**

| Type | Genitive | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ο** | **-ου** — του βιβλίου | **ου** |
| **-ι** | **-ιού** — **του παιδιού, του σπιτιού** | **ιού, with the stress on the ending** |
| **-μα** | **-ματος** — του γράμματος | |
| **-ος** | **-ους** — του μέρους | |

**του παιδιού is the form to know**, because the **-ι** neuters are everywhere and their genitive moves the stress: **το σπίτι → του σπιτιού**, **το παιδί → του παιδιού**, **το χέρι → του χεριού**.

**The plural:**

| Type | Plural | Spelling point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-ο** | **-α** — τα βιβλία | **α** |
| **-ι** | **-ια** — τα παιδιά, τα σπίτια | **ια** |
| **-μα** | **-ματα** — τα γράμματα, τα μαθήματα | **ατα** |
| **-ος** | **-η** — **τα μέρη, τα δάση, τα έθνη** | **η — and this is the awkward one** |
| **-ιμο** | **-ίματα** — τα κλεισίματα | |

**τα μέρη with -η is the neuter's one real trap.** The neuter **-ος** nouns — **το μέρος, το δάσος, το έθνος, το κράτος, το βάρος, το τέλος, το λάθος, το ήθος, το πάθος, το μέγεθος** — all make their plural in **-η**, which sounds like an *i* and is spelt eta.

> **το λάθος → τα λάθη**
> **το κράτος → τα κράτη**
> **το έθνος → τα έθνη**

**And their genitive plural is -ων on a changed stem**: **των μερών, των κρατών, των εθνών**.

**The accusative: identical to the nominative, in both numbers.** That is the neuter's gift, and it means half the decisions disappear.

**The genitive plural: -ων throughout**, as everywhere — **των βιβλίων, των παιδιών, των γραμμάτων, των μερών**.

**The three full tables:**

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom./Acc.** | το βιβλίο | τα βιβλία |
| **Gen.** | του βιβλίου | των βιβλίων |

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom./Acc.** | το παιδί | τα παιδιά |
| **Gen.** | του παιδιού | των παιδιών |

| | Singular | Plural |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom./Acc.** | το μάθημα | τα μαθήματα |
| **Gen.** | του μαθήματος | των μαθημάτων |

**The spelling summary for the neuter, in four lines:**

1. **Singular in -ι is always iota.**
2. **Singular in -ο is always omicron.**
3. **Plural in -α, -ια or -ατα is always alpha.**
4. **Plural in -η belongs to the -ος nouns, and is always eta.**

**Practice.** Write the three tables above from memory. Then list ten **-ι** neuters and write their genitive singulars with the stress moved. Then list the ten **-ος** neuters above and write their plurals in **-η**.
The genitive, in all three genders:
One lesson on one case, because the genitive is the case written Greek uses most and the case whose endings a learner most often gets wrong.

**Why it earns a lesson of its own.** Stage 9 showed that formal Greek runs on genitive chains — **η ανακοίνωση της απόφασης της κυβέρνησης** — so every nominalised phrase, every **λόγω**, every **σύμφωνα με**, and every possessive in the language needs a correctly spelt genitive.

**The genitive singular, every pattern, in one table:**

| Gender and type | Nominative | Genitive | Spelling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M. -ος** | ο άνθρωπος | **του ανθρώπου** | **-ου** |
| **M. -ης** | ο μαθητής | **του μαθητή** | **-η**, no ς |
| **M. -ας** | ο πατέρας | **του πατέρα** | **-α** |
| **M. -έας** | ο ιερέας | **του ιερέα** | **-α** |
| **M. -ους** | ο παππούς | **του παππού** | **-ού** |
| **F. -η** | η νίκη | **της νίκης** | **-ης** |
| **F. -α** | η ώρα | **της ώρας** | **-ας** |
| **F. -ση** | η απόφαση | **της απόφασης** | **-ης**, and **-εως** in the learned register |
| **F. -ος** | η οδός | **της οδού** | **-ού** |
| **N. -ο** | το βιβλίο | **του βιβλίου** | **-ου** |
| **N. -ι** | το παιδί | **του παιδιού** | **-ιού**, stress on the ending |
| **N. -μα** | το γράμμα | **του γράμματος** | **-ατος** |
| **N. -ος** | το μέρος | **του μέρους** | **-ους** |

**The four errors this table prevents:**

1. **του μαθητής** — wrong. The **-ης** genitive drops the **ς**: **του μαθητή**.
2. **της νίκη** — wrong. The feminine genitive **adds** a **ς**: **της νίκης**.
3. **του παιδιού** — and learners write **του παιδίου** by analogy with **βιβλίου**. The **-ι** neuters take **-ιού**.
4. **του γράμματου** — wrong. The **-μα** nouns take **-ατος**.

**The genitive plural: -ων, with no exceptions worth the name.**

> **των ανθρώπων, των μαθητών, των γυναικών, των παιδιών, των γραμμάτων, των μερών, των πόλεων**

**Always omega. Always -ων.** Note that the stress usually moves to the ending, and that **των πόλεων** keeps a learned **-εων**.

**The article, which must agree and which is itself a spelling test:**

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Gen. sg.** | **του** | **της** | **του** |
| **Gen. pl.** | **των** | **των** | **των** |

**του with omicron, των with omega.** Those two are among the commonest words in the language and the contrast is worth drilling: **του ανθρώπου** against **των ανθρώπων**.

**The possessive clitics**, which are genitives and which are spelt as they sound:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **μου, σου, του, της, μας, σας, τους** | and all of them unaccented, after the noun |
| **το σπίτι μου** | my house |
| **ο πατέρας της** | her father |

**Note του and τους here are the clitics**, written identically to the article forms, and distinguished only by position.

**The drill that fixes the genitive**, and it is the most productive single drill in the Spelling track:

**Take any noun phrase and make it genitive after a preposition.**

> το σπίτι → **λόγω του σπιτιού**
> η απόφαση → **μετά την ανακοίνωση **της απόφασης****
> οι άνθρωποι → **η γνώμη **των ανθρώπων****
> τα μαθήματα → **το πρόγραμμα **των μαθημάτων****

**Say the ending's reason aloud each time**: *neuter -ι, so -ιού.*

**Practice.** Take twenty nouns from today's reading, in all three genders, and write each one's genitive singular and plural. Check against the table. Then build five genitive chains two deep, of the kind stage 9's nominalisation lesson used.
The plurals, in all three genders:
The other half of the noun's spelling, in one place — and the lesson that resolves the commonest *i* and *e* choices in the language.

**The nominative plural, every pattern:**

| Gender and type | Singular | Plural | Spelling |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **M. -ος** | ο άνθρωπος | **οι άνθρωποι** | **-οι** |
| **M. -ης** | ο μαθητής | **οι μαθητές** | **-ες** |
| **M. -ας** | ο πατέρας | **οι πατέρες** | **-ες** |
| **M. -έας** | ο ιερέας | **οι ιερείς** | **-είς**, learned |
| **M. -ωνας** | ο αγώνας | **οι αγώνες** | **-ες** |
| **F. -η** | η νίκη | **οι νίκες** | **-ες** |
| **F. -α** | η ώρα | **οι ώρες** | **-ες** |
| **F. -ση** | η απόφαση | **οι αποφάσεις** | **-εις** |
| **F. -ος** | η οδός | **οι οδοί** | **-οί** |
| **N. -ο** | το βιβλίο | **τα βιβλία** | **-α** |
| **N. -ι** | το παιδί | **τα παιδιά** | **-ιά** |
| **N. -μα** | το γράμμα | **τα γράμματα** | **-ατα** |
| **N. -ος** | το μέρος | **τα μέρη** | **-η** |

**The four plural endings that sound alike and are spelt differently**, which is the whole problem:

| Sound | Spellings | Which is which |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ***-i*** | **-οι** / **-εις** / **-η** / **-οί** | masculine **-ος** → **-οι**; feminine **-ση** → **-εις**; neuter **-ος** → **-η**; feminine **-ος** → **-οί** |
| ***-es*** | **-ες** / **-αις** | **always -ες** in modern Greek; **-αις** is katharevousa |
| ***-a*** | **-α** / **-ια** / **-ατα** | by the singular's ending |

**The decision procedure, in three questions**, which is how to use this in practice:

1. **What gender is it?**
2. **What is its singular ending?**
3. **Read the plural off the table.**

**And the four high-frequency cases to know cold:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **οι άνθρωποι, οι δρόμοι, οι λόγοι** | masculine **-ος** → **-οι** |
| **οι αποφάσεις, οι πόλεις, οι δυνάμεις** | feminine **-ση/-ξη/-ψη** → **-εις** |
| **τα λάθη, τα κράτη, τα έθνη** | neuter **-ος** → **-η** |
| **τα παιδιά, τα σπίτια, τα χέρια** | neuter **-ι** → **-ιά / -ια** |

**The accusative plural**, which is where the masculine differs:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Masculine** | **-ους** — τους ανθρώπους; **-ες** — τους μαθητές |
| **Feminine** | **the same as the nominative** — τις νίκες, τις πόλεις |
| **Neuter** | **the same as the nominative** — τα βιβλία, τα παιδιά |

**τους ανθρώπους with -ους is the masculine accusative plural** and the one form that is not shared: **οι άνθρωποι** (nominative) against **τους ανθρώπους** (accusative).

**The articles in the plural, which agree and must be spelt right:**

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom.** | **οι** | **οι** | **τα** |
| **Gen.** | **των** | **των** | **των** |
| **Acc.** | **τους** | **τις** | **τα** |

**οι with omicron-iota** for both masculine and feminine nominative plural — and **it is not ι, not η, and not εί.** It is the commonest two-letter word in the language and worth being certain of.

**The irregular plurals worth knowing**, because they recur:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **ο άντρας → οι άντρες** | regular, but watch the stem |
| **η γυναίκα → οι γυναίκες** | and genitive plural **των γυναικών** |
| **το κρέας → τα κρέατα** | |
| **το φως → τα φώτα** | |
| **το γάλα → τα γάλατα** | |
| **ο παππούς → οι παππούδες** | |
| **η μητέρα → οι μητέρες** | |
| **το γεγονός → τα γεγονότα** | |
| **ο καφές → οι καφέδες** | |

**Practice.** Write the plural of thirty nouns from today's reading, naming the gender and the singular ending aloud each time. Then check that every feminine **-ση** became **-σεις**, every neuter **-ος** became **-η**, and every masculine **-ος** became **-οι**.
The adjective endings:
Adjectives agree in gender, number and case, which means every adjective ending is a spelling decision — and there are five patterns.

**Pattern 1: -ος / -η / -ο**, the main one:

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom. sg.** | **καλός** | **καλή** | **καλό** |
| **Gen. sg.** | **καλού** | **καλής** | **καλού** |
| **Acc. sg.** | **καλό** | **καλή** | **καλό** |
| **Nom. pl.** | **καλοί** | **καλές** | **καλά** |
| **Gen. pl.** | **καλών** | **καλών** | **καλών** |
| **Acc. pl.** | **καλούς** | **καλές** | **καλά** |

**The four *i*-sounding forms in that table**, which is where the errors are:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **καλή** | feminine nominative and accusative singular — **η** |
| **καλοί** | masculine nominative plural — **οι** |
| **καλής** | feminine genitive singular — **ης** |
| **καλοί / καλή** | and nothing here is ever **-ι** or **-ει** |

**Pattern 2: -ος / -α / -ο**, where the stem ends in a vowel or **ρ**:

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom. sg.** | **ωραίος** | **ωραία** | **ωραίο** |
| **Nom. pl.** | **ωραίοι** | **ωραίες** | **ωραία** |

**The feminine is -α, not -η**, when the stem ends in a vowel: **ωραίος → ωραία, νέος → νέα, παλιός → παλιά, κρύος → κρύα**. The working rule: **-ιος, -ειος, -οιος** and **-αιος** take **-α**; everything else takes **-η**, including the **-ρος** adjectives — **μικρός → μικρή, καθαρός → καθαρή**.

**Pattern 3: -ύς / -ιά / -ύ**, a small and very common group:

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom. sg.** | **βαθύς** | **βαθιά** | **βαθύ** |
| **Nom. pl.** | **βαθιοί** | **βαθιές** | **βαθιά** |

**The group is small and closed**: **βαθύς, βαρύς, μακρύς, φαρδύς, πλατύς, ελαφρύς, παχύς, δασύς**. **The -ύ is upsilon**, which is the spelling point, and **γλυκός** is not a member — it follows pattern 1.

**Pattern 4: -ης / -ια / -ι**, the colour and quality adjectives:

| | M. | F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom. sg.** | **σταχτής** | **σταχτιά** | **σταχτί** |

**And the neuter is -ί with iota**: **θαλασσί, καφετί, πορτοκαλί, σταχτί, βυσσινί**. These are the colour words formed from nouns.

**Pattern 5: -ης / -ης / -ες**, the learned two-termination adjectives:

| | M./F. | N. |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Nom. sg.** | **διεθνής** | **διεθνές** |
| **Gen. sg.** | **διεθνούς** | **διεθνούς** |
| **Nom. pl.** | **διεθνείς** | **διεθνή** |

**The group is large in written Greek**: **διεθνής, ευγενής, συνεχής, ακριβής, επιμελής, ασφαλής, πλήρης, συγγενής, ειδής-compounds**. **The -είς plural with epsilon-iota** and the **-ούς genitive** are the forms to recognise.

**The participial adjective, -μένος**, which declines like pattern 1:

> **γραμμένος, γραμμένη, γραμμένο — γραμμένοι, γραμμένες, γραμμένα**

**The comparative and superlative spellings:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **-ότερος** | **καλός → καλύτερος** (irregular), **μεγάλος → μεγαλύτερος**, **ωραίος → ωραιότερος** |
| **-ύτερος** | after some stems — **καλύτερος, μεγαλύτερος** |
| **πιο + adjective** | the analytic form, and the commonest in speech |
| **-ότατος** | the absolute superlative — **ωραιότατος, μέγιστος** |

**The one rule that catches most adjective errors.** **Find the noun, name its gender, number and case, and give the adjective the same.** An adjective never has a spelling of its own — it has the noun's.

**Practice.** Take ten noun-plus-adjective phrases from today's reading and name the gender, number and case of each. Then decline **καλός**, **ωραίος**, **βαθύς** and **διεθνής** in full, and check the four *i*-sounding forms of each.
Spelling drill: the noun in a sentence:
The module's drill, which is the whole point of it: the ending decided from the grammar, at speed, in a sentence.

**How the drill works.** A sentence with the ending blanked. You fill it in and **say the reason out loud**. The reason is what transfers.

**Set one — the *i* endings:**

| Sentence | Answer and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Η καλ__ γυναίκα ήρθε. | **καλή** — feminine nominative singular |
| Οι καλ__ άνθρωποι φεύγουν. | **καλοί** — masculine nominative plural |
| Είδα τις πόλ__. | **πόλεις** — feminine **-ση** type, accusative plural |
| Τα λάθ__ ήταν πολλά. | **λάθη** — neuter **-ος** type, plural |
| Της καλ__ γυναίκας. | **καλής** — feminine genitive singular |
| Ο μαθητ__ διαβάζει. | **μαθητής** — masculine nominative singular |
| Του μαθητ__ το βιβλίο. | **μαθητή** — masculine **-ης** genitive, no **ς** |

**Set two — the genitives:**

| Sentence | Answer and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Λόγω του παιδ__. | **παιδιού** — neuter **-ι**, genitive **-ιού** |
| Η πόρτα του σπιτ__. | **σπιτιού** — same |
| Το νόημα του γράμμα__. | **γράμματος** — neuter **-μα**, genitive **-ατος** |
| Μετά την ανακοίνωση της απόφασ__. | **απόφασης** — feminine, genitive adds **ς** |
| Η γνώμη των ανθρώπ__. | **ανθρώπων** — genitive plural, **-ων** |
| Στην άκρη της οδ__. | **οδού** — feminine **-ος** type |

**Set three — the plurals:**

| Singular | Plural and reason |
| --- | --- |
| ο δρόμος | **οι δρόμοι** — masculine **-ος** → **-οι** |
| η απόφαση | **οι αποφάσεις** — **-ση** → **-εις** |
| το κράτος | **τα κράτη** — neuter **-ος** → **-η** |
| το σπίτι | **τα σπίτια** — neuter **-ι** → **-ια** |
| το μάθημα | **τα μαθήματα** — **-μα** → **-ατα** |
| η γυναίκα | **οι γυναίκες** — feminine **-α** → **-ες** |
| ο ιερέας | **οι ιερείς** — **-έας** → **-είς**, learned |

**Set four — the whole phrase**, which is the real test. Write each phrase in the case asked for, article and adjective included:

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| *the good man*, genitive singular | **του καλού ανθρώπου** |
| *the good women*, accusative plural | **τις καλές γυναίκες** |
| *the big decisions*, nominative plural | **οι μεγάλες αποφάσεις** |
| *the little children*, genitive plural | **των μικρών παιδιών** |
| *the international organisations*, nominative plural | **οι διεθνείς οργανισμοί** |
| *because of the bad weather*, genitive | **λόγω της κακοκαιρίας** |

**The dictation drill, which is the strongest version**, from Spelling 1's hand lesson and stage 9's: **play two sentences of a podcast and write them.** Then check against the transcript and classify every error:

| Error type | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **An ending** | you did not name the grammar. Redo it aloud. |
| **A root *i*** | card the word. |
| **An accent** | count the accents on the page. |
| **Final -ν** | reread Spelling 1's rule. |
| **A double consonant** | card the word; Spelling 4 has the patterns. |

**The honest target.** After this module, **ending errors should be close to zero** and your remaining errors should be roots, accents and double consonants — which are memory and which the next two modules address.

**The weekly habit for the track.** Twenty minutes, twice a week: one set of these drills, and one dictation of four sentences. **That is the whole Spelling track in practice**, and it is why his answer was "drills bruh".

**Practice.** Do all four sets above, writing the answers and saying the reasons aloud. Then do a four-sentence dictation and classify every error by the table. The largest category tells you which lesson to reread.
The verb endings, and the -ει problem:
The second half of the endings' leverage, and the single most frequent spelling error in Greek — made by learners and by native speakers alike.

**The error, stated first.** The third person singular of a verb is **-ει**. Always. In every mood.

> **γράφει** — *he writes*
> **να γράφει** — *that he write*
> **θα γράφει** — *he will be writing*
> **να γράψει** — *that he write (perfective)*
> **θα γράψει** — *he will write*

**-η is never a verb ending in modern Greek.** The form **να γράφη** existed in katharevousa, where the subjunctive had its own spelling, and the 1976 reform abolished it. **Writing να γράφη is the commonest orthographic error in the language.**

**And the mirror error**, which is just as common: writing **-ει** where a **noun** needs **-η**.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **η νίκη** | the victory — **noun, so -η** |
| **νικεί** | he wins — **verb, so -ει** |
| **η τιμή** | the price, the honour — noun |
| **τιμά** | he honours — verb |
| **η ζωή** | life — noun |
| **ζει** | he lives — verb |

**So the decision procedure is one question: is it a verb?** If yes, third person singular is **-ει**. If no, the noun and adjective rules from the last module apply.

**The six person endings of the present active**, which are the most-written letters in the language:

| Person | Ending | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1 sg.** | **-ω** | γράφ**ω** |
| **2 sg.** | **-εις** | γράφ**εις** |
| **3 sg.** | **-ει** | γράφ**ει** |
| **1 pl.** | **-ουμε** | γράφ**ουμε** |
| **2 pl.** | **-ετε** | γράφ**ετε** |
| **3 pl.** | **-ουν** | γράφ**ουν** |

**The four spelling points in that table:**

1. **-ω with omega** in the first person. Never **-ο**.
2. **-εις with epsilon-iota** in the second person. Never **-ης**.
3. **-ει with epsilon-iota** in the third. Never **-η**, never **-ι**.
4. **-ουμε and -ουν with ου.** Never **-ομε**, never **-oυμαι**.

**The -ω / -ο contrast is worth a moment**, because it recurs:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γράφω** | I write — verb, omega |
| **το βιβλίο** | the book — neuter noun, omicron |
| **καλό** | good — neuter adjective, omicron |
| **μιλώ** | I speak — verb, omega |

**The rule: a verb's first person is -ω; a neuter's singular is -ο.** Both are everywhere and the contrast never varies.

**-ετε against -εται**, which is the other classic confusion:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γράφετε** | *you (pl.) write* — **active, second person plural** |
| **γράφεται** | *it is written* — **passive, third person singular** |

**They sound identical in modern Greek.** The grammar is the only guide: **-ετε** has a plural subject doing something, **-εται** has a singular subject having something done to it. **This is the second most common Greek spelling error after να γράφη.**

**The test**: can you put **εσείς** in front of it? Then **-ετε**. Can you put **αυτό**? Then **-εται**.

> **Εσείς γράφετε το γράμμα.**
> **Το γράμμα γράφεται.**

**Practice.** Write out the six present endings of **γράφω**, **μιλώ** and **διαβάζω**. Then take twenty verbs from today's reading and name the person of each, checking the ending. Then write ten sentences alternating **-ετε** and **-εται**, saying which is which.
The present and the -άω verbs:
The two conjugations' spellings, because the **-άω / -ώ** verbs have endings that look nothing like the **-ω** verbs' and are just as common.

**Conjugation 1: the -ω verbs**, stress on the stem:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γράφω, γράφεις, γράφει, γράφουμε, γράφετε, γράφουν** | and the same for διαβάζω, παίρνω, θέλω, ξέρω, τρώω… |

**Conjugation 2a: the -άω / -ώ verbs**, stress on the ending, type **αγαπώ**:

| Person | Form | Alternative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1 sg.** | **αγαπώ** | αγαπάω |
| **2 sg.** | **αγαπάς** | |
| **3 sg.** | **αγαπά** | αγαπάει |
| **1 pl.** | **αγαπάμε** | αγαπούμε |
| **2 pl.** | **αγαπάτε** | |
| **3 pl.** | **αγαπούν** | αγαπάνε |

**The spelling points:**

1. **αγαπώ with omega**, like all first persons.
2. **αγαπάς, αγαπά, αγαπάμε, αγαπάτε with alpha** — **and no -ει anywhere.** The third person singular of this conjugation is **αγαπά** or **αγαπάει**, never **αγαπεί**.
3. **αγαπούν with ου.**
4. **The alternatives are both correct** and both written; **αγαπάει** is commoner in speech.

**Conjugation 2b: the -ώ verbs of the other type**, type **μπορώ**:

| Person | Form |
| --- | --- |
| **1 sg.** | **μπορώ** |
| **2 sg.** | **μπορείς** |
| **3 sg.** | **μπορεί** |
| **1 pl.** | **μπορούμε** |
| **2 pl.** | **μπορείτε** |
| **3 pl.** | **μπορούν** |

**And here the endings are -εις, -εί, -είτε with epsilon-iota** — so this conjugation looks like conjugation 1 in the second and third persons, and the first person is **-ώ** with the stress on it.

**The members of each type, because you have to know which a verb is:**

| 2a (**-άω**) | 2b (**-ώ**) |
| --- | --- |
| αγαπώ, μιλώ, ρωτώ, περνώ | μπορώ, θεωρώ, τηλεφωνώ, συμφωνώ |
| γελώ, πεινώ, διψώ, ξεχνώ | αργώ, κινώ, ζητώ… |
| χαλώ, σταματώ, κρατώ | προχωρώ, οδηγώ, ευχαριστώ |
| φυλώ, βαστώ, πετώ | καλώ, μισώ, νικώ, τιμώ |

**ζητώ, κρατώ and a number of others take both sets**, which is why dictionaries list the forms. **The Triantafyllidis dictionary gives them, and Lexiscope will inflect any verb you are unsure of.**

**The verbs you cannot guess:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **είμαι** | είμαι, είσαι, είναι, είμαστε, είστε, είναι — **and είναι is the only -αι in the set** |
| **έχω** | regular conjugation 1 |
| **πάω** | πάω, πας, πάει, πάμε, πάτε, πάνε |
| **λέω** | λέω, λες, λέει, λέμε, λέτε, λένε |
| **τρώω** | τρώω, τρως, τρώει, τρώμε, τρώτε, τρώνε |
| **ξέρω** | regular, and no perfective |

**είναι is worth the note** because it is the commonest word in the language and it is spelt **-αι**, which looks like a passive ending and is not.

**The imperfect**, which has its own endings and its own spellings:

| Conjugation | Imperfect |
| --- | --- |
| **1 (-ω)** | **έγραφα, έγραφες, έγραφε, γράφαμε, γράφατε, έγραφαν** |
| **2a (-άω)** | **αγαπούσα, αγαπούσες, αγαπούσε, αγαπούσαμε, αγαπούσατε, αγαπούσαν** |
| **2b (-ώ)** | **μπορούσα, μπορούσες, μπορούσε…** |

**The -ούσα endings of conjugation 2 are all ου**, and the **έ-** at the front of **έγραφα** is the augment, which the next lesson covers.

**Practice.** Conjugate **μιλώ**, **μπορώ** and **διαβάζω** in the present, in full, from memory. Then list ten verbs from today's reading and say which conjugation each belongs to. Then check three of them in Lexiscope.
The past endings, and the augment:
The past tense's spellings, which are simpler than the present's — and the one feature of Greek that moves the accent onto a syllable that was not there before.

**The past endings, the same for the aorist and the imperfect:**

| Person | Ending | Aorist | Imperfect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **1 sg.** | **-α** | έγραψ**α** | έγραφ**α** |
| **2 sg.** | **-ες** | έγραψ**ες** | έγραφ**ες** |
| **3 sg.** | **-ε** | έγραψ**ε** | έγραφ**ε** |
| **1 pl.** | **-αμε** | γράψ**αμε** | γράφ**αμε** |
| **2 pl.** | **-ατε** | γράψ**ατε** | γράφ**ατε** |
| **3 pl.** | **-αν** | έγραψ**αν** | έγραφ**αν** |

**The spelling points, and there are only three:**

1. **Every past ending has alpha or epsilon**, and none has an *i*. **So the past tense is the easiest part of the verb to spell.**
2. **-ες and -ε with epsilon** — not **-αις**, which is katharevousa.
3. **-αν, and also -ανε** as a spoken alternative: **έγραψαν / γράψανε**.

**The difference between the aorist and the imperfect is the stem, not the ending** — **έγραψα** against **έγραφα** — which is why the Forms track's lesson on perfective stems matters for spelling.

**The augment: the ε- at the front.**

Greek puts an **έ-** before the stem in the past when the verb would otherwise have no syllable to carry the stress:

> **γράφω → έγραψα** — the stress must fall on the third syllable from the end, and **γράψα** has only two, so **ε-** is added.
> **γράφω → γράψαμε** — three syllables already, so no augment.

**The rule, stated as a rule:** the past tense's stress falls on the **third syllable from the end**. If the word does not have three, an **ε-** is prefixed to make one.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **έγραψα, έγραψες, έγραψε, έγραψαν** | two-syllable stems, so the augment appears |
| **γράψαμε, γράψατε** | three syllables already, so no augment |
| **διάβασα, διάβασες, διάβασε** | the stem is long enough; the stress just moves back |
| **διαβάσαμε, διαβάσατε** | and moves forward again |

**So the augment appears in four of the six persons and vanishes in two**, which looks strange and is entirely mechanical.

**The spelling of the augment is always ε** — **έγραψα, έφυγα, είδα, ήπια**… and two verbs take **η-** instead, which is a survival:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **ήθελα** | from θέλω |
| **ήξερα** | from ξέρω |
| **ήμουν** | from είμαι |
| **ήπια** | from πίνω |
| **ήρθα** | from έρχομαι |

**Those five take η- and they are all very common**, so they are worth learning as a set rather than deriving.

**The learned augment**, which you will read and not write: katharevousa and Koine use **ε-** inside compound verbs, where modern Greek puts it at the front or omits it:

| Learned | Modern |
| --- | --- |
| **ανεχώρησε** | **αναχώρησε** |
| **ενεγράφη** | **γράφτηκε** |
| **εγένετο** | **έγινε** |

**You will meet those in church and legal texts.** Recognise them; the classical curriculum explains them.

**The one real spelling trap in the past tense.** The third person plural has two forms and the accent differs:

> **έγραψαν** — augment, stress on the augment
> **γράψανε** — no augment, stress on the stem

**Both are correct.** The first is the written norm; the second is spoken and appears in dialogue.

**Practice.** Write the aorist and the imperfect of **γράφω**, **διαβάζω** and **μιλώ** in full, marking where the augment appears and where it does not. Then write the five **η-** verbs' past forms. Then find ten past-tense verbs in today's reading and say for each whether it has an augment and why.
The perfective stems, spelt:
The spelling consequences of the aorist stem, which is where the **-σ-, -ψ-, -ξ-** choices come from and where most of the remaining verb errors live.

**What the perfective stem is**, from stage 4: every Greek verb has two stems, and the perfective one is used for the aorist, the perfective future, the perfective subjunctive and the perfective imperative. **Its spelling is a fact about the verb**, like a root *i*.

**The three regular formations:**

| Stem ends in | Perfective marker | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **a vowel, or ν, ζ, θ, δ, τ** | **-σ-** | **λύνω → έλυσα**; **διαβάζω → διάβασα**; **αγοράζω → αγόρασα**; **ακούω → άκουσα** |
| **π, β, φ, πτ, υ** | **-ψ-** | **γράφω → έγραψα**; **κρύβω → έκρυψα**; **κόπτω → έκοψα**; **δουλεύω → δούλεψα** |
| **κ, γ, χ, γγ, σσ, ζ** | **-ξ-** | **ανοίγω → άνοιξα**; **τρέχω → έτρεξα**; **πλέκω → έπλεξα**; **αλλάζω → άλλαξα** |

**So the marker is decided by the consonant it meets**, exactly as in Ancient Greek, and the three groups are:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **The labials** (π β φ, and -εύω) | give **ψ** |
| **The velars** (κ γ χ) | give **ξ** |
| **Everything else** | gives **σ** |

**ζ is the awkward one** and goes both ways: **διαβάζω → διάβασα** but **αλλάζω → άλλαξα**. It is a fact about each verb.

**The high-frequency perfectives worth knowing cold:**

| Verb | Perfective | Marker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **γράφω** | **γράψω** | ψ |
| **δουλεύω** | **δουλέψω** | ψ |
| **μαγειρεύω** | **μαγειρέψω** | ψ |
| **ανοίγω** | **ανοίξω** | ξ |
| **τρέχω** | **τρέξω** | ξ |
| **αλλάζω** | **αλλάξω** | ξ |
| **παίζω** | **παίξω** | ξ |
| **διαβάζω** | **διαβάσω** | σ |
| **αγοράζω** | **αγοράσω** | σ |
| **ακούω** | **ακούσω** | σ |
| **αρχίζω** | **αρχίσω** | σ |
| **μιλώ** | **μιλήσω** | σ, with **-ήσ-** |
| **αγαπώ** | **αγαπήσω** | **-ήσ-** |
| **ρωτώ** | **ρωτήσω** | **-ήσ-** |
| **μπορώ** | **μπορέσω** | **-έσ-** |
| **τηλεφωνώ** | **τηλεφωνήσω** | **-ήσ-** |

**The -ήσω / -έσω group is the conjugation-2 pattern**, and the spelling point is the **η** in **-ήσω**: **αγαπήσω, μιλήσω, ρωτήσω, περπατήσω, σταματήσω**. **It is eta, and it is regular for the -άω verbs.**

**The conjugation-2b verbs take -έσω**: **μπορέσω, καλέσω** — **epsilon** — and a few take **-ήσω** as well. The dictionary decides.

**The irregular perfectives, which must be learned one by one.** The commonest fifteen:

| Verb | Perfective | Aorist |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **βλέπω** | **δω** | **είδα** |
| **λέω** | **πω** | **είπα** |
| **πηγαίνω / πάω** | **πάω** | **πήγα** |
| **παίρνω** | **πάρω** | **πήρα** |
| **βρίσκω** | **βρω** | **βρήκα** |
| **μπαίνω** | **μπω** | **μπήκα** |
| **βγαίνω** | **βγω** | **βγήκα** |
| **έρχομαι** | **έρθω** | **ήρθα** |
| **δίνω** | **δώσω** | **έδωσα** |
| **τρώω** | **φάω** | **έφαγα** |
| **πίνω** | **πιω** | **ήπια** |
| **φεύγω** | **φύγω** | **έφυγα** |
| **μένω** | **μείνω** | **έμεινα** |
| **στέλνω** | **στείλω** | **έστειλα** |
| **θέλω** | — | **ήθελα** (no perfective) |

**The spelling points in that list**: **δω, πω, βρω, μπω, βγω, πιω** are monosyllables with no marker at all; **μείνω** and **στείλω** take **ει**; **είδα** and **είπα** take **ει**.

**The -ει- in έμεινα and έστειλα is worth flagging** because it is a root *i* that most learners get wrong: **μένω → έμεινα**, **στέλνω → έστειλα**, and also **πλένω → έπλυνα** with **υ**.

**Practice.** For thirty verbs from today's reading, write the perfective stem and name the marker and why. Then write out the fifteen irregulars from memory, and check the **ει** spellings. Then run any verb you are unsure of through Lexiscope.
The passive endings:
The passive's spellings, which have their own set of endings and one pair that is the second commonest error in Greek.

**The present passive, every person:**

| Person | Ending | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1 sg.** | **-μαι** | γράφο**μαι** |
| **2 sg.** | **-σαι** | γράφε**σαι** |
| **3 sg.** | **-ται** | γράφε**ται** |
| **1 pl.** | **-μαστε** | γραφό**μαστε** |
| **2 pl.** | **-στε** | γράφε**στε** |
| **3 pl.** | **-νται** | γράφο**νται** |

**Every one of those is spelt -αι in the three persons that end in a vowel sound**: **-μαι, -σαι, -ται, -νται.** **Never -ε, never -ε ι.** That is the single rule of the passive present.

**And the error, restated from the first lesson of this module:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γράφετε** | *you (pl.) write* — active |
| **γράφεται** | *it is written* — passive |

**Identical in sound. The test is the subject**: **εσείς γράφετε**, **αυτό γράφεται**.

**The same pair for every verb**, and it is worth drilling as pairs:

| Active 2 pl. | Passive 3 sg. |
| --- | --- |
| **διαβάζετε** | **διαβάζεται** |
| **λέτε** | **λέγεται** |
| **θεωρείτε** | **θεωρείται** |
| **πιστεύετε** | **πιστεύεται** |
| **απαγορεύετε** | **απαγορεύεται** |

**θεωρείτε against θεωρείται is the hardest of them** and both are common in written Greek — *you consider* against *it is considered* — and stage 9's impersonal list is full of the second.

**The imperfect passive:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γραφόμουν, γραφόσουν, γραφόταν, γραφόμαστε, γραφόσαστε, γραφόντουσαν / γράφονταν** | |

**All with ο and ου**, and no *i* sounds — so the imperfect passive is easy to spell and awkward to say.

**The aorist passive**, which is the form you will write most:

| Ending | Example | Group |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **-θηκα** | **αγαπήθηκα, θεωρήθηκα, ανακοινώθηκα** | the **-ώθηκα / -ήθηκα** verbs |
| **-τηκα** | **γράφτηκα, κόπηκα, χάθηκα** | the **-φ-, -π-** stems |
| **-χτηκα** | **ανοίχτηκα, διώχτηκα** | the velar stems |
| **-στηκα** | **στάθηκα, πλύστηκα** | some **-σ-** stems |

**The person endings are the ordinary past ones**: **-ηκα, -ηκες, -ηκε, -ήκαμε, -ήκατε, -ηκαν.**

**And the spelling point is the η**: **-θηκα, -τηκα, -χτηκα** all have **eta**, never iota. **γράφτηκε, ανακοινώθηκε, εγκρίθηκε** — all eta.

**The passive subjunctive and future**, which take the perfective passive stem:

> **να γραφτώ, να γραφτείς, να γραφτεί** — **and -εί with epsilon-iota**, like every third person singular
> **θα γραφτεί** — the future
> **να ανακοινωθεί, θα εγκριθεί** — the **-θεί** forms, very common in written Greek

**να ανακοινωθεί with -θεί is one of the most-written forms in formal Greek** and the **ει** is the ordinary third-person ending. **Not -θή**, which is katharevousa.

**The perfect passive**, which uses **έχω** plus an invariable form:

> **έχω γραφτεί, έχει ανακοινωθεί, είχε εγκριθεί**

**And the participle, -μένος**, which declines like an adjective and whose spelling is **-μένος** with epsilon: **γραμμένος, κλεισμένος, αγαπημένος, κουρασμένος**.

**The deponents**, which look passive and are not, and which you must spell as passives:

**έρχομαι, κάθομαι, σκέφτομαι, αισθάνομαι, φοβάμαι, θυμάμαι, χρειάζομαι, εργάζομαι, ασχολούμαι, αποτελούμαι, χειρίζομαι, κοιμάμαι, λυπάμαι**

**All of them take -μαι, -σαι, -ται**, so **έρχεται, σκέφτεται, φοβάται, θυμάται** — **and none of them is ever -ετε**, because they have no active.

**Practice.** Write the present passive of **γράφομαι** and **σκέφτομαι** in full. Then write ten **-ετε / -εται** pairs and say which is which. Then write the aorist passive of **ανακοινώνω**, **εγκρίνω** and **γράφω**, checking every eta.
The subjunctive, which has no spelling o:
A short lesson on a frequent worry: **να** plus a verb is spelt exactly as the verb is spelt. There is no subjunctive spelling in modern Greek.

**The statement.** Modern Greek has no distinct subjunctive forms. What grammars call the subjunctive is **να** or another particle plus the ordinary indicative endings, in one aspect or the other.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **να γράφω** | imperfective — *that I write, keep writing* |
| **να γράψω** | perfective — *that I write, once* |
| **θα γράφω** | imperfective future |
| **θα γράψω** | perfective future |
| **ας γράψω** | let me write |
| **να μην γράψω** | negative — **μην**, not **δεν** |

**And every one of those uses the same six endings** from the first lesson of this module: **-ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν.**

**So there is nothing new to spell**, and the historical reason this needs saying is that katharevousa **did** have a separate subjunctive spelling:

| Katharevousa | Modern |
| --- | --- |
| **ίνα γράφη** | **να γράφει** |
| **να γράφωμεν** | **να γράφουμε** |
| **να γραφή** | **να γραφεί** |

**The old forms used -η and -ω where the modern uses -ει and -ουμε**, and because the Church's texts and older books are full of them, the forms are still in the air. **They are wrong in modern writing.**

**The three particles and their spellings:**

| Particle | Spelling point |
| --- | --- |
| **να** | plain alpha |
| **θα** | plain alpha, and **never θά** — it is unaccented |
| **ας** | plain |
| **μην / μη** | **η**, and **μην** before a vowel or a stop |
| **δεν / δε** | **ε**, and **δεν** before a vowel or a stop |

**δεν against μην is a grammar question with a spelling consequence:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **δεν** | negates the indicative — **δεν γράφω, δεν έγραψα, δεν θα γράψω** |
| **μην** | negates everything with **να**, and the imperative — **να μην γράψω, μην γράφεις** |

**The imperative, which is the one place with its own endings:**

| | Imperfective | Perfective |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **2 sg.** | **γράφε** | **γράψε** |
| **2 pl.** | **γράφετε** | **γράψτε** |

**And the negative imperative uses να μην or μην**: **μην γράφεις**, **να μην γράψεις** — **there is no negative imperative form.**

**The spelling of the perfective imperative plural** is worth noting: **γράψτε, διαβάστε, πάρτε, πείτε, δώστε, ελάτε** — all **-τε**, with the perfective stem and a consonant cluster.

**The one genuinely irregular set:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **έλα / ελάτε** | come |
| **πες / πείτε** | say |
| **δες / δείτε** | look |
| **πάρε / πάρτε** | take |
| **δώσε / δώστε** | give |
| **φάε / φάτε** | eat |
| **πιες / πιείτε** | drink |
| **μπες / μπείτε** | come in |
| **βγες / βγείτε** | go out |
| **ανέβα / ανεβείτε** | come up |
| **κατέβα / κατεβείτε** | come down |

**Note the ει in πείτε, δείτε, πιείτε, μπείτε, βγείτε** — epsilon-iota, as in every second-person plural.

**Practice.** Write the four aspect-and-tense combinations of **γράφω**, **διαβάζω** and **μιλώ** — **να γράφω, να γράψω, θα γράφω, θα γράψω** — and check that nothing is spelt with **-η**. Then write the eleven irregular imperatives from memory.
Spelling drill: the verb in a sentence:
The verb module's drill, in the same shape as the noun module's: the ending decided from the grammar, at speed, with the reason said aloud.

**Set one — the -ει problem:**

| Sentence | Answer and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Θέλω να γράφ__ κάθε μέρα. | **γράφει** — third person singular, always **-ει** |
| Η νίκ__ ήταν εύκολη. | **νίκη** — feminine noun, **-η** |
| Αυτός νικ__ πάντα. | **νικά** (or **νικάει**) — conjugation 2a, **-ά** |
| Πρέπει να πάμε, μη ξεχάσ__. | **ξεχάσεις** — second person singular, **-εις** |
| Θα ανακοινωθ__ αύριο. | **ανακοινωθεί** — passive third singular, **-θεί** |
| Μπορ__ να με βοηθήσεις; | **Μπορείς** — conjugation 2b, **-είς** |

**Set two — -ετε against -εται:**

| Sentence | Answer and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Εσείς τι διαβάζ__; | **διαβάζετε** — *you* plural, active |
| Το βιβλίο διαβάζ__ εύκολα. | **διαβάζεται** — *it*, passive |
| Θεωρ__ ότι είναι σωστό; | **Θεωρείτε** — *you* plural, active |
| Θεωρ__ ότι είναι σωστό. | **Θεωρείται** — impersonal passive |
| Απαγορεύ__ το κάπνισμα. | **Απαγορεύεται** — impersonal passive |
| Γιατί δεν απαντ__; | **απαντάτε** — *you* plural, conjugation 2a |

**Set three — the past, and the augment:**

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| γράφω, 1 sg. aorist | **έγραψα** — augment, two-syllable stem |
| γράφω, 1 pl. aorist | **γράψαμε** — three syllables, no augment |
| διαβάζω, 3 sg. aorist | **διάβασε** — stress back, no augment needed |
| θέλω, 1 sg. imperfect | **ήθελα** — the **η-** group |
| έρχομαι, 1 sg. aorist | **ήρθα** — the **η-** group |
| μένω, 1 sg. aorist | **έμεινα** — **ει** in the stem |
| στέλνω, 1 sg. aorist | **έστειλα** — **ει** in the stem |

**Set four — the perfective markers:**

| Verb | Perfective, and why |
| --- | --- |
| γράφω | **γράψω** — labial φ, so **ψ** |
| δουλεύω | **δουλέψω** — **-εύω**, so **ψ** |
| ανοίγω | **ανοίξω** — velar γ, so **ξ** |
| τρέχω | **τρέξω** — velar χ, so **ξ** |
| διαβάζω | **διαβάσω** — **σ** |
| αλλάζω | **αλλάξω** — **ξ**, and ζ goes both ways |
| μιλώ | **μιλήσω** — conjugation 2a, **-ήσω** with eta |
| μπορώ | **μπορέσω** — conjugation 2b, **-έσω** with epsilon |

**Set five — the whole sentence.** Write each in Greek, then check every verb ending:

| Ask | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| *You (pl.) write well.* | **Γράφετε καλά.** |
| *It is written in the book.* | **Γράφεται στο βιβλίο.** |
| *I want you to come tomorrow.* | **Θέλω να έρθεις αύριο.** |
| *It was announced yesterday.* | **Ανακοινώθηκε χθες.** |
| *We had already read it.* | **Το είχαμε διαβάσει ήδη.** |
| *Don't say anything.* | **Μην πεις τίποτα.** |
| *It is forbidden to smoke here.* | **Απαγορεύεται το κάπνισμα εδώ.** |

**The error log, which is the point of the drill.** Classify every mistake:

| Error | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **-η for -ει** | you did not ask whether it was a verb |
| **-ετε for -εται** | you did not find the subject |
| **Wrong perfective marker** | learn the three consonant groups |
| **Missing or wrong augment** | count the syllables |
| **-θή for -θεί** | a katharevousa form; it is wrong in modern writing |
| **Wrong conjugation** | check the verb in Lexiscope and card it |

**The weekly habit, restated.** Twenty minutes twice a week: one drill set, and one four-sentence dictation. **After both modules of endings, your spelling errors should be roots and accents only** — which is what Spelling 4 and 5 are for.

**Practice.** Do all five sets. Then take a paragraph you wrote in stage 9 and check every verb against the six endings and the **-ετε / -εται** test. Then do a four-sentence dictation and log the errors by type.
Double consonants:
The first of the root-spelling problems: which words take a double letter, when there is no sound difference at all in standard Greek.

**The fact.** Standard Modern Greek pronounces **λλ, μμ, νν, ππ, σσ, ττ, ρρ, κκ, γγ** as single consonants. **άλλος** sounds like *alos*; **θάλασσα** like *thalasa*. So the doubling is pure orthography, inherited from Ancient Greek, and it has to be learned word by word.

**The exception, from stage 10**: Cypriot pronounces them long, as the ancients did. **So if you have heard a Cypriot say ούλλος or θάλασσα, you have heard the doubling** — which is a genuine aid to memory.

**The words with double letters**, by letter — and this is most of the burden:

| Double | Words |
| --- | --- |
| **λλ** | **άλλος, αλλά, πολλοί, μάλλον, Ελλάδα, Έλληνας, ελληνικά, φύλλο, μέλλον, συλλογή, σύλλογος, παράλληλος, κολλάω, καλλιτέχνης, έλλειψη** |
| **μμ** | **γράμμα, γραμματική, πρόγραμμα, γραμμή, άμμος, κομμάτι, κόμμα, σύμμαχος** |
| **νν** | **έννοια, εννοώ, γέννηση, γεννάω, γενναίος, εννιά, συννεφιά, Άννα, Γιάννης** |
| **ππ** | **παππούς, ίππος, ιππότης, Φίλιππος, Ιπποκράτης** |
| **σσ** | **θάλασσα, γλώσσα, μέλισσα, τέσσερα, περισσότερο, περισσεύω** |
| **γγ** | **άγγελος, άγγελμα, αγγίζω, Αγγλία, αγγλικά, φεγγάρι, εγγονός, εγγύηση, συγγραφέας** |
| **κκ** | **εκκλησία, εκκίνηση, κόκκινος, κόκκαλο** |
| **ρρ** | **άρρωστος, άρρητος, παρρησία, συρράπτης** |
| **ββ** | **Σάββατο, Σάββας** — and these are nearly the only ones |
| **ττ** | **Αττική**, and little else in modern Greek |

**The high-value set, which is the one to actually drill** — the words you will write most:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Ελλάδα, Έλληνας, ελληνικά** | double λ, and you will write these constantly |
| **εκκλησία** | **double κ** — the single most important one for your purposes |
| **άλλος, αλλά, πολλοί, μάλλον** | double λ |
| **γράμμα, πρόγραμμα, γραμμή, κόμμα** | double μ |
| **θάλασσα, γλώσσα, περισσότερο** | double σ |
| **άγγελος, Αγγλία, αγγλικά, συγγραφέας, φεγγάρι** | **γγ** |
| **έννοια, γέννηση, Γιάννης, εννιά** | double ν |
| **παππούς** | double π |
| **άρρωστος** | double ρ |
| **κόκκινος** | double κ |

**εκκλησία is worth a sentence of its own.** It is **εκ** + **κλησία** — *called out* — so the double kappa is a prefix boundary, and once you see that, you cannot misspell it.

**And that is the one real rule in this area: a double letter is often a prefix meeting a stem.**

| Compound | Result |
| --- | --- |
| **εκ + κλησία** | **εκκλησία** |
| **συν + γραφέας** | **συγγραφέας** |
| **εν + νοια** | **έννοια** |
| **συν + ράπτω** | **συρράπτης** |
| **παν + νυχίς** | **παννυχίς / πανηγύρι** |

**The next lesson is about those prefixes**, and between them the prefix rule and a hundred cards cover almost all of it.

**The words that look as though they should double and do not** — worth knowing because the error runs both ways:

**τόσο, όσο, πόσο, μέσα, ίσως, χώρα, κότα, πίτα, Λάρισα, καλός, φίλος**, and two pairs that catch everyone:

| One letter | Two letters |
| --- | --- |
| **πολύ** — very, much | **πολλοί, πολλά, πολλές** — many |
| **μέλι** — honey | **μέλλον** — the future |

**πολύ against πολλοί is the pair to get straight:** **πολύ** (*very, much*) has one lambda; **πολλοί / πολλά / πολλές** (*many*) have two. **And the Cypriot πολλά meaning *very* from stage 10 has two**, because it is the same word as *many*.

**The method.** There is no shortcut. **Card every double-consonant word you get wrong**, front Greek, back the meaning, and note on the card that it is a spelling card. Fifty cards covers the words you will actually write.

**Practice.** Write the ten high-value words above from dictation — have the list read to you, or read it aloud and write from memory. Then take a page you have written and check every λ, μ, σ, ν and γγ. Then card every one you got wrong.
The prefixes, and how they assimilate:
The one systematic part of Greek root spelling: prefixes have fixed spellings, they change predictably when they meet a consonant, and knowing twenty of them explains thousands of words.

**Why this is the best-value lesson in the module.** Greek builds vocabulary by compounding, so a very large part of the learned and technical lexicon is **prefix + stem**. **If you know the prefix, you know the spelling of the first half of the word** — and you often know its meaning too.

**The prepositional prefixes, with their spellings and senses:**

| Prefix | Sense | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ανα-** | up, again | **ανάσταση, αναφορά, αναγνωρίζω, ανακοίνωση** |
| **αντι-** | against, instead of | **αντίθεση, αντιγράφω, αντίδωρο, αντιπρόσωπος** |
| **απο-** | from, away, completion | **απόφαση, αποστέλλω, αποτέλεσμα, απολογία** |
| **δια-** | through | **διαβάζω, διάλογος, διαμονή, διαδικασία** |
| **εν-** | in | **ένταση, έννοια, ενδιαφέρον, ενορία** |
| **εκ- / εξ-** | out of | **έκθεση, εκκλησία, εξέλιξη, εξομολόγηση** |
| **επι-** | on, upon | **επίσκοπος, επιστολή, επιτροπή, επίδραση** |
| **κατα-** | down, thoroughly | **κατάσταση, κατηχητικό, καταλαβαίνω, κατάλογος** |
| **μετα-** | after, change | **μετάνοια, μεταφορά, μεταξύ, μετάβαση** |
| **παρα-** | beside, past | **παράδοση, παρακαλώ, παράκληση, παρουσία** |
| **περι-** | around | **περιοχή, περίοδος, περιγραφή, περιβάλλον** |
| **προ-** | before | **πρόγραμμα, πρόσφυγας, προσευχή, πρόβλημα** |
| **προς-** | towards | **προσφορά, πρόσκληση, προσπάθεια** |
| **συν-** | with, together | **σύνοδος, συγγραφέας, συμμετοχή, σύλλογος** |
| **υπερ-** | over, excessive | **υπερβολή, υπερήφανος, υπέρβαση** |
| **υπο-** | under, slightly | **υπογραφή, υπόθεση, υποχρέωση, υπομονή** |

**The spelling points, in four lines:**

1. **αντι- is iota.** Not **αντη-**, not **αντει-**.
2. **επι-, περι-, προ-, υπο- are all iota or omicron** and never vary.
3. **υπερ- and υπο- are upsilon**, which is the one prefix with a *y*.
4. **συν- and εν- change shape**, which is the next part.

**The assimilation of συν- and εν-**, which is mechanical and explains a great many spellings:

| Before | συν- becomes | εν- becomes | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **π, β, φ, ψ, μ** | **συμ-** | **εμ-** | **συμπέρασμα, συμβούλιο, συμφωνία, σύμμετρος; έμπειρος, εμφάνιση** |
| **κ, γ, χ, ξ** | **συγ-** | **εγ-** | **συγκέντρωση, συγγραφέας, συγχαρητήρια; εγκύκλιος, έγκριση** |
| **λ** | **συλ-** | **ελ-** | **σύλλογος, συλλογή, συλλαβή; έλλειψη** |
| **ρ** | **συρ-** | **ερ-** | **συρράπτης** |
| **σ** | **συσ- / συ-** | | **σύσταση, σύστημα** |
| **anything else** | **συν-** | **εν-** | **σύνοδος, συντακτικό; έντονος, ενδιαφέρον** |

**The two to notice:**

- **συγγραφέας** has **γγ** because **συν** + **γραφέας** assimilated — which also explains **σύγγραμμα, συγγενής, συγκατάθεση**.
- **εκκλησία** has **κκ** because **εκ** + **κλησία** assimilated, from the last lesson.

**So the double-consonant problem and the prefix problem are the same problem**, and the prefix is the key to it.

**εκ- against εξ-**, which is simple:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **εξ-** | before a vowel — **εξέλιξη, εξομολόγηση, εξαίρεση, εξαρχής** |
| **εκ-** | before a consonant — **έκθεση, εκδήλωση, εκλογή, εκκλησία** |

**The negative and intensive prefixes:**

| Prefix | Sense | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **α- / αν-** | not | **άδικος, άγνωστος, ανίκανος, αναίμακτος** |
| **δυσ-** | badly | **δυστυχία, δύσκολος, δυσκολία** |
| **ευ-** | well | **ευτυχία, ευχαριστώ, ευλογία, ευαγγέλιο** |
| **ημι-** | half | **ημικύκλιο, ημιτελής** |
| **φιλο- / μισο-** | loving / hating | **φιλοξενία, φιλόσοφος, μισάνθρωπος** |
| **αυτο-** | self | **αυτοκίνητο, αυτονομία, αυτοκράτορας** |
| **πολυ- / ολιγο-** | many / few | **πολυκατοικία, ολιγαρχία** |
| **παν- / παμ-** | all | **πανηγύρι, Παναγία, παμψηφεί** |

**ευ- is the one with a spelling trap**: it is **ευ**, the digraph, pronounced *ev* before a voiced sound and *ef* before a voiceless one — **ευχαριστώ** (*ef-*), **ευλογία** (*ev-*). **Both spelt ευ.**

**And α- against αν-**: **αν-** before a vowel (**ανίκανος, ανώμαλος, ανέξοδος**), **α-** before a consonant (**άδικος, άγνωστος, άτοπος**).

**The practical payoff.** When you meet an unknown long Greek word, **split off the prefix first.** **αναγνωρίζω** = **ανα** + **γνωρίζω** = *recognise again*. **υπογραφή** = **υπο** + **γραφή** = *under-writing*, a signature. **Nine times in ten the word becomes transparent**, and its spelling becomes derivable rather than arbitrary.

**Practice.** Take twenty long words from today's reading and split each into prefix and stem. Then write the assimilated forms of **συν-** and **εν-** before each of the consonant groups. Then spell **εκκλησία, συγγραφέας, σύλλογος, συμβούλιο, εγκύκλιος** from memory and say which prefix each contains.
The root spellings, by pattern:
The irreducible part: the *i*, *e* and *o* spellings inside roots. There is no rule — but there are patterns, and the patterns cut the memory load by half.

**The honest statement first.** Whether **τιμή** takes iota and **νίκη** takes iota and **τύχη** takes upsilon is a fact inherited from Ancient Greek. **You cannot derive it.** What follows is not a rule system but a set of regularities that make the cards stick.

**Pattern 1: η in abstract nouns from verbs.**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **-η** | **τιμή, νίκη, αγάπη, γραφή, αρχή, ευχή, προσευχή, τροφή, ψυχή, βροχή** |

**A great many feminine abstract nouns take η**, and their verbs often take a different vowel: **τιμή / τιμώ, νίκη / νικώ, γραφή / γράφω**.

**Pattern 2: ι in neuter diminutives and concrete things.**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **-ι** | **παιδί, σπίτι, χέρι, πόδι, μάτι, αυτί, ψωμί, κρασί, κλειδί, τραπέζι, μαχαίρι, πιρούνι** |

**Every neuter in -ι is iota**, from Spelling 2 — so this pattern is already covered by the endings rule.

**Pattern 3: υ in words of Greek learned origin.**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **υ** | **τύχη, ύλη, ύψος, φύση, γλυκός, κρύος, λύση, μύθος, ρυθμός, σύστημα, φύλλο, ξύλο, μύτη, νύχτα, πύλη, δύναμη, θυμός, κύριος, ψυχή** |

**The υ words are worth learning as a group**, because they are numerous and because **υ** is the least-guessed of the *i* spellings. **A word that looks learned or abstract and has an *i* sound in the stem is quite often υ.**

**Pattern 4: ει inside a root — a list, not a rule.**

There is no way to predict **ει**, and the set of common words that take it is small enough to learn:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **ει** | **είμαι, είναι, είδα, είπα, εκείνος, ειρήνη, εικόνα, είσοδος, σχολείο, κλειδί, κλείνω, μείνω, στείλω, δείχνω, λείπω, γείτονας, τελειώνω, εμπειρία, τείχος, χείλος** |

**Twenty words, carded as a set, covers nearly every **ει** you will need to write.** Note that **έξοδος** takes omicron despite **είσοδος** taking **ει** — which is the kind of thing that confirms there is no rule here.

**Pattern 5: αι against ε — and here there is one real rule.**

**Verbs in -αίνω take αι, every one of them:**

> **μαθαίνω, πεθαίνω, ανεβαίνω, κατεβαίνω, πηγαίνω, ζεσταίνω, παθαίνω, τυχαίνω, φαίνομαι, χαίρομαι**

**That is a genuine pattern and worth having**, because the **-αίνω** verbs are common and the ending recurs.

**Outside the -αίνω verbs, αι is a list:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **αι** | **και, ναι, είναι, παιδί, παίζω, παίρνω, αίμα, αιτία, αιώνας, καιρός, γυναίκα, αίθουσα, δαίμονας, Αιγαίο** |

**And the reliable rule in this area is grammatical**, from Spelling 3: **-αι is a passive verb ending (γράφεται)** and **-ε is an active one (γράφετε)**. Inside a root, use the list and the dictionary.

**Pattern 6: ο against ω.**

**Here there is a usable rule**, and it is the best thing in this lesson:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **-ω** | **first person of a verb** — γράφω, μιλώ |
| **-ο** | **neuter noun or adjective singular** — το βιβλίο, καλό |
| **-ος** | **masculine nominative** — ο άνθρωπος |
| **-ων** | **genitive plural** — των ανθρώπων |

**Inside a root**, **ω** is commoner in learned vocabulary: **ώρα, χώρα, σώμα, φως, ζωή, γνώση, πρώτος, μεγάλωνω, δώρο, χρώμα, πρόσωπο, ανώνυμος** — and **ο** is commoner in everyday words: **πόλη, πόδι, λόγος, κόσμος, όνομα, μόνος**.

**That is a tendency and not a rule**, and the honest advice is the same: cards.

**The method for this lesson, which is the method for the whole problem:**

1. **Apply the endings rules first** — Spelling 2 and 3. They settle most of it.
2. **Split off the prefix** — the last lesson. That settles the first half of long words.
3. **What remains is the root**, and for the root: **guess, check in Triantafyllidis, card it if you were wrong.**
4. **Learn the υ group deliberately**, because it is the one list that repays being learned as a list.

**And one mechanical aid.** When you look a word up, **look at its etymology line** in the Triantafyllidis dictionary. **τύχη < τυγχάνω** explains the upsilon; **τιμή < τίω** explains the iota. **The etymology is the mnemonic**, and it is free with every lookup.

**Practice.** Learn the twenty **υ** words above. Then take fifteen words from today's reading whose root spelling you would have had to guess, look each one up, and read its etymology line. Then card the five you got wrong.
Homophones, and spelling as meaning:
The place where spelling carries meaning rather than merely recording sound — and the one part of Greek orthography that is genuinely useful rather than merely traditional.

**The principle.** Greek has many pairs that sound identical and are spelt differently, and the spelling is the only thing distinguishing them. **In these cases the orthography is doing real work**, and getting it wrong changes the meaning rather than merely looking careless.

**The accent pairs, from stage 1's accent lesson**, which are the same phenomenon with a mark instead of a letter:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **πότε** (when?) | **ποτέ** (never) |
| **πού** (where?) | **που** (that, who) |
| **πώς** (how?) | **πως** (that) |
| **ή** (or) | **η** (the) |
| **άλλα** (other things) | **αλλά** (but) |
| **γέρος** (old man) | **γερός** (strong) |
| **νόμος** (law) | **νομός** (prefecture) |
| **μόνος** (alone) | **μονός** (single, odd) |

**The letter pairs:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **τείχος** (a wall, of a city) | **τύχη** (luck) — and **τοίχος** (a wall, of a room) |
| **λίπος** (fat) | **λείπω** (I am absent) |
| **κλίνω** (I incline, I decline a noun) | **κλείνω** (I close) |
| **λιμός** (famine) | **λοιμός** (plague) |
| **φιλί** (a kiss) | **φυλή** (a tribe, a race) |
| **τοίχος** (wall of a house) | **τείχος** (city wall) |
| **πείρα** (experience) | **πύρα** (heat) |
| **σήμα** (a sign) | **σύμα** — not a word; but **σώμα** (body) |
| **λύρα** (lyre) | **λίρα** (pound sterling) |
| **ίσως** (perhaps) | **ίσος** (equal) |
| **στήλη** (a column) | **στύλος** (a pillar) |
| **πηγή** (a spring, a source) | **πυγή** — and the distinction matters |

**τοίχος against τείχος is the pair to know**, because both are walls and the difference is real: **ο τοίχος** is the wall of a room or a house; **το τείχος** is a fortification — the walls of Constantinople are **τα Τείχη**.

**κλίνω against κλείνω is the other**, and it is a grammarian's word against an everyday one: **κλίνω ένα ουσιαστικό** is *I decline a noun*; **κλείνω την πόρτα** is *I close the door*.

**The verb pairs from Spelling 3**, restated because they belong here:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **γράφετε** (you write) | **γράφεται** (it is written) |
| **θεωρείτε** (you consider) | **θεωρείται** (it is considered) |
| **να γράφει** (correct) | **να γράφη** (katharevousa, wrong) |

**The words that differ only by a breathing in the old system** and are now identical — worth knowing because the Church's texts keep the breathings:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **ὅρος** (boundary) | **ὄρος** (mountain) — modern Greek: **όρος** and **όρος**, distinguished only by context |
| **ἔξω** (outside) | **ἕξω** (I shall have) |

**Those collapsed when the polytonic was abolished in 1982**, which is one of the arguments its defenders make, and it is worth knowing that the argument has this much substance.

**The practical approach:**

1. **The accent pairs must be learned** — there are about ten and they are high-frequency. **Card them as pairs**, not singly.
2. **The letter pairs are mostly learned vocabulary** and can be learned as they arise.
3. **The verb pairs are grammar** and are settled by the tests in Spelling 3.

**And one reassurance.** Greeks confuse these too — **τοίχος / τείχος** and **κλίνω / κλείνω** are standard examples in Greek school textbooks because Greek children get them wrong. **Getting them right marks careful writing rather than being a basic requirement.**

**The loanword question**, which belongs here because it is also spelling-as-meaning:

**How does Greek spell an imported word?** By convention, and the conventions have changed. **The modern rule is simplification**:

| Older | Current |
| --- | --- |
| **τραίνο** | **τρένο** |
| **αυτοκίνητον** | **αυτοκίνητο** |
| **σαιζόν** | **σεζόν** |
| **πουλόβερ** | unchanged |
| **κομπιούτερ / υπολογιστής** | and Greek prefers the Greek word |

**The 1976 reform's principle is that loanwords are spelt as simply as the sound allows** — single consonants, **ε** rather than **αι**, **ι** rather than **ει** or **υ**. **So μπάσκετ, φαξ, ίντερνετ, σάντουιτς, γκολ, τένις** — all spelt plainly.

**The exception is a name**, which keeps its conventional spelling: **Σαίξπηρ, Βολταίρος** alongside the modern **Σέξπιρ**. Both appear.

**Practice.** Card the ten accent pairs as pairs. Then write a sentence for each member of **τοίχος / τείχος** and **κλίνω / κλείνω**. Then find five loanwords in today's reading and notice how plainly they are spelt.
Spelling drill: dictation:
The module's drill and the best single exercise in the Spelling track: writing down Greek you hear, and classifying every error.

**Why dictation is the right test.** It is the only exercise that tests all five spelling problems at once:

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **The endings** | which you must derive from the grammar you hear |
| **The root *i*, *e* and *o*** | which you must know |
| **The accent** | which you must place |
| **Final -ν** | which you must decide |
| **Double consonants** | which you must remember |

**And it tests listening at the same time**, which is why stage 9's handwriting lesson called it the best combined drill in the curriculum.

**The method, four steps:**

1. **Choose two to four sentences** of audio you can follow — a podcast with a transcript, an Ellinomatheia listening paper, a sentence from an audiobook with the text, or the Easy Greek podcast.
2. **Play it twice**, writing as you go. By hand.
3. **Play it a third time** to check.
4. **Compare against the transcript and classify every error.**

**The error log, which is the whole value:**

| Error type | What it tells you | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **An ending** | you did not name the grammar | redo it aloud, with the reason — Spelling 2 or 3 |
| **A root *i*/*e*/*o*** | you do not know the word's spelling | card it |
| **A missing accent** | habit | count the accents on your page, every time |
| **A misplaced accent** | you do not know the word's stress | card it with the stress marked |
| **Final -ν** | the rule | reread Spelling 1 |
| **A double consonant** | memory | card it |
| **A word you could not hear** | listening, not spelling | that is stage 8's problem, not this one |

**Keep the log.** Four columns — date, error, type, fixed — and after a month the distribution tells you exactly where your remaining spelling burden is. **It is usually roots and accents, which means cards.**

**The graded dictation material, free:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Ellinomatheia listening papers** | **graded A1–C2 with audio and transcripts.** The best dictation material available, and matched to the curriculum's levels. |
| **Easy Greek's podcast** | with transcripts, at two speeds |
| **Omilo's short pieces** | with text |
| **The daily saint, read aloud** | if you can find audio — formulaic, so the second week is easier |
| **An audiobook with the text** | a paragraph at a time |
| **Someone at church** | **the best version**: ask one person to read you four sentences |

**That last one is worth doing once.** Asking a Greek to dictate four sentences is a thirty-second favour, it produces natural speech rather than recorded speech, and it is a conversation.

**Self-dictation, which works when nothing else is available.** Read a paragraph aloud, close the book, write it from memory, then compare. **It is not as good as hearing someone else, and it is better than nothing** — and it drills the same five things.

**The copying drill, from stage 9's imitation lesson**, which is dictation's gentler cousin: copy a paragraph out by hand. **It teaches the same spellings without testing them**, so it is the right exercise when dictation is discouraging.

**The weekly shape of the whole Spelling track, settled:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Twice a week, twenty minutes** | one lesson's drill set, from Spelling 2 or 3 |
| **Once a week** | a four-sentence dictation, with the error log |
| **Once a week** | a paragraph copied by hand |
| **Continuously** | the deck, with every spelling card you have made |

**Two sessions and two short drills a week.** That is what "drills bruh" amounts to in practice, and it is forty minutes.

**The target, stated honestly.** Not perfect spelling — Greeks do not have perfect spelling. **The target is: no ending errors, accents placed, and a known list of root words you keep getting wrong, on cards.** That is achievable within a year of this track and it is what careful writing requires.

**Practice.** Do a four-sentence dictation today from an Ellinomatheia paper or the Easy Greek podcast. Classify every error in the log's four columns. Then card every root and accent error. Then do it again next week and compare the distribution.
